Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding molten salt thermal energy storage costs:

## Cost Estimates

For molten chloride salt thermal energy storage systems, the cost of the TES system is estimated to be $60/kWhth, though this represents research from 2021 and is higher than DOE targets.

For earlier nitrate salt systems, molten nitrate salt costs were reported at 22-30 $/kWhth (based on historical data from Solar Two and other plants).

## Future Cost Projections

Looking toward 2025, the transition to molten salt HTF in trough plants could halve the installed cost of storage in molten-salt parabolic trough plants by 2025, with installed TES costs expected to fall to $16/kWh-thermal by 2025, according to IRENA.

## DOE Goals

The Gen3 CSP program targets an energy cost of 5 cents per kWh, which represents NREL and DOE's next-generation goals for concentrated solar power systems overall.

Note: The search results contain older NREL reports on molten salt cost modeling (from 2013) rather than specific 2025 data, and the most recent technical studies focus on molten chloride salts as an advanced alternative to traditional nitrate salts.

Based on the search results, here are the latest utility-scale lithium-ion BESS installed cost figures for 2025-2026:

## All-In Project Costs (October 2025)

Across global markets outside China and the United States, the total capex to build a large, long-duration utility-scale BESS project is around $125/kWh, comprising $75/kWh for the core equipment shipped from China and around $50/kWh for installation and grid connection. This represents real-world project prices derived from recent auction results in Saudi Arabia, India and Italy, as well as interviews conducted in October 2025 with experts working on BESS projects across global markets.

## Regional Variation

Cost breakdown:
- The price of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery cells for stationary energy storage applications has dropped to around $40/kWh in Chinese domestic markets as of November 2025.
- On a regional basis, average battery pack prices were lowest in China, at $94/kWh.
- Packs in the US and Europe were 31% and 48% higher, reflecting the relative immaturity of these markets, as well as higher production costs and lower volumes.

## China Market Pricing

In 2025, BESS system pricing reached new lows with project tenders in China falling to as low as $63/kWh. However, the pricing environment has shifted at the start of the new year, with lithium prices surging to a two-year high, driven by tightening inventories, mine production slowdowns, robust demand, and most recently China's rollback of battery tax rebates.

content.text:
## Setting up the physics

**Medium:** "solar salt" (60% NaNO₃ / 40% KNO₃), the standard CSP TES fluid.
- Operating range: 290 °C (cold tank) → 565 °C (hot tank), ΔT = 275 K
- cp ≈ 1.5 kJ/kg·K, density ≈ 1,800–2,100 kg/m³

Energy density: ΔT·cp = 275 × 1.5 = 412.5 kJ/kg = **0.1146 kWh_th/kg** → ≈8.7 kg of salt per kWh_th stored.

For 5 MWh = 5,000 kWh_th: **salt mass ≈ 43.6 tonnes**, split across two tanks each sized to hold the full inventory (two-tank design: at full charge all salt sits in the hot tank, at full discharge all of it sits in the cold tank). Each tank volume ≈ 25–28 m³ — roughly a 3 m-diameter, 4 m-tall vessel. This is a genuinely small system; CSP-scale TES is usually hundreds to thousands of MWh.

## Bottom-up capital cost build

| Component | Basis | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Salt inventory | 43.6 t × ~$1,000/t (no bulk discount at this scale) | $44,000 |
| Hot tank (565 °C, alloy/refractory-lined) + cold tank (carbon steel) | small specialty vessels, heat-traced, insulated | $200,000 |
| Salt-rated heat exchanger train | ~1 MW_th charge/discharge duty, corrosion-resistant alloys | $250,000 |
| Salt pumps (hot + cold, cantilever/sealless) | 2 units | $120,000 |
| Piping, valves, freeze-protection heat tracing | salt freezes ≈220 °C — mandatory trace heating | $100,000 |
| Additional insulation | tanks + piping | $50,000 |
| Instrumentation & controls | temp/level/flow, freeze-protection logic | $100,000 |
| Electrical (heat-trace power, switchgear) | | $80,000 |
| Foundations/civil, bunding | | $100,000 |
| **Equipment + materials subtotal** | | **≈$1.04M** |
| Installation labor (~30%) | | $313,000 |
| EPC/engineering/PM (~20% of above) | | $271,000 |
| Contingency (~15%) | | $247,000 |
| **Total installed capital cost** | | **≈$1.9M** |

**≈ $380/kWh_th** installed capacity.

This is checked against real benchmarks: large utility CSP two-tank nitrate systems historically run **$22–30/kWh_th** (Solar Two-era), trending toward IRENA's projected **~$16/kWh_th** at gigawatt-hour scale. My $380/kWh_th is ~15–25× higher, and that gap is structurally correct, not an error: tank cost scales with shell *surface area* (~volume^(2/3)) while capacity scales with *volume*, and the pumps/HX/controls/engineering costs are nearly fixed regardless of size. A 5 MWh system pays almost the same fixed-cost tax as a 500 MWh one. Molten-salt sensible-heat storage is a technology whose economics only work at large scale — at 5 MWh it's essentially a one-off/pilot unit.

## Amortizing over cycle life

Molten salt has no electrochemical wear-out mechanism — life is set by tank fatigue/corrosion, typically **25–30 years**, ≈1 cycle/day → **~9,000–10,000 cycles**.

Two very different use cases matter here:

**(a) Pure thermal storage** (heat in, heat out — e.g., paired directly with a solar field or process-heat source, no power-cycle round trip): recovery efficiency ~95–98% (mostly standby/HX losses).
- LCOS ≈ $380 / (9,500 × 0.97) ≈ **$0.041/kWh_th delivered** (capital only, excl. O&M/financing)

**(b) "Carnot battery" mode** (electricity → resistive heating → salt → steam Rankine → electricity), the only way to compare directly against Li-ion since Li-ion stores and returns electricity: round-trip efficiency is ~40–45% for a simple resistive-charge/steam-discharge design.
- Effective capacity in $/kWh-electric = $380 / 0.425 ≈ $894/kWh_e
- LCOS ≈ $894 / 9,500 ≈ **$0.094/kWh_e delivered**

## Lithium-ion comparison

Current (late-2025) utility-scale BESS all-in installed costs have fallen sharply — around **$125/kWh** in competitive global markets (cells ex-China ~$75/kWh + ~$50/kWh install/interconnect), with US/Europe project costs running ~30–50% above that, say **$150–220/kWh** for a small 5 MWh project once soft costs are included. AC-AC round-trip efficiency ~88–92%. Calendar/cycle life typically **4,000–6,000 cycles** (often calendar-life-limited, ~10–15 years).

- LCOS ≈ $180 / (5,000 × 0.90) ≈ **$0.040/kWh_e delivered**

## Verdict

- As a **direct heat-storage** device, the molten-salt system's amortized cost (~$0.04/kWh_th) is in the same ballpark as Li-ion's amortized electric cost — but that's not a fair fight, since Li-ion can't substitute for storing/returning heat directly; nothing is being "competed" here.
- As a **standalone electricity-storage asset** (the only genuinely comparable case), molten salt comes out to roughly **$0.09–0.10/kWh delivered** versus Li-ion's **~$0.03–0.04/kWh delivered** — Li-ion wins by **roughly 2.5–3×**, driven almost entirely by (1) the double energy-conversion penalty of power-to-heat-to-power and (2) the brutal small-scale capital penalty molten salt pays below CSP-plant scale.
- At the scale where molten-salt TES actually makes sense (hundreds of MWh+, bundled with a CSP solar field so there's no electric round-trip conversion at all), its economics flip and it becomes genuinely cheaper than batteries for multi-hour-to-multi-day duration — which is exactly why it's used that way in practice and essentially never built as a 5 MWh standalone unit.

**Bottom line:** at 5 MWh, molten-salt TES is not cost-competitive with lithium-ion for electricity storage — it's roughly 3× more expensive per kWh delivered, mainly because this scale is far below molten salt's economic sweet spot and because converting electricity→heat→electricity throws away over half the energy. Molten salt only wins once you're at CSP-plant scale and storing heat directly, not electricity.

Sources:
- [Molten Salt Power Tower Cost Model for SAM (NREL)](https://research-hub.nrel.gov/en/publications/molten-salt-power-tower-cost-model-for-the-system-advisor-model-s/)
- [Technical and Economic Feasibility of Molten Chloride Salt TES (NREL)](https://research-hub.nrel.gov/en/publications/technical-and-economic-feasibility-of-molten-chloride-salt-therma-2/)
- [Developing a Cost Model and Methodology to Estimate Capital Costs for TES (OSTI)](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1031953)
- [All-in BESS projects now cost just $125/kWh as of October 2025 (Ember Energy)](https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/how-cheap-is-battery-storage/)
- [Li-ion BESS costs could fall 47% by 2030, NREL long-term forecast](https://energy-storage.news/li-ion-bess-costs-could-fall-47-by-2030-nrel-says-in-long-term-forecast-update)
